item.title: 42 BGB platoons deployed in Dhaka, Gazipur, Narayanganj
item.description:
A total of 42 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) have been deployed in industrial areas across Dhaka, Gazipur and Narayanganj to maintain law and order and ensure public safety, according to BGB headquarters.
Of the deployed personnel, 20 platoons are in Dhaka, covering Mirpur, Savar, Hemayetpur and Ashulia, including areas near Yunus Convention Hall, Kathgara, Zirabo, Hameem Group, Midlar Group and Jamgara.
Another 15 platoons have been deployed in Gazipur, covering Chandra, Palli Bidyut, Mouchak, Konabari, Telirchala, Kashimpur, Bhogra Bypass, Gacha, Sataish and Salna.
The remaining seven platoons are stationed in Narayanganj, covering Shibu Market, Katherpul, Jalkuri, the BSCIC Industrial Estate, Chashara Mor, Kanchpur Bridge and Shimrail.
BGB headquarters is conducting continuous, technology-driven surveillance to monitor developments on the ground and coordinate operations, the force said.
The monitoring includes real-time footage from drones, body-worn cameras and other specialised equipment.
The BGB said it remains on high alert in coordination with the local administration and police to maintain law and order, ensure public safety and respond to any untoward incidents in the industrial zones.
The force added that it is maintaining constant surveillance and taking necessary measures as the situation evolves.

item.title: Minimum wage protest halts traffic in Mirpur

item.title: Crude bomb explodes at Mirpur Model Police Station
item.description:

However, Officer-in-Charge Hafizur Rahman said sound grenades had been deployed in response to a protest by garment workers, adding that the loud noise heard in the area was caused by the detonation of the grenades.

item.title: Police, BGB fire tear gas, sound grenades as Gazipur workers block roads
item.description:
Workers from several factories staged protests in Gazipur's Joydebpur and Chandana Chowrasta areas on Tuesday, demanding an increase in the minimum wage.
Their road blockades since the morning disrupted traffic on the Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway, Joydebpur Road and Bhogra Bypass.
Police and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) members fired tear gas shells and sound grenades to bring the situation under control, triggering chases and counter-chases between workers and law enforcers
However, the workers refused to leave the roads despite the measures.
Workers also attempted to block the Dhaka-Tangail Highway in the Naojor area over the same demand. Law enforcers later removed them from the road.
According to police and local sources, workers from several factories in Joydebpur and Chandana Chowrasta began protesting around 9am without joining their shifts. Hundreds of workers from different factories later gathered and took positions on the roads.
At one stage, they blocked the Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway and Joydebpur Road, bringing traffic to a standstill.
Police and BGB members went to the scene and asked the workers to clear the roads. The situation soon escalated, leading to chases and counter-chases between the two sides.
Law enforcers later fired tear gas shells and sound grenades in an attempt to disperse the workers, but they continued their blockade.
Mohammad Amzad Hossain, superintendent of police of Gazipur Industrial Zone-2, said workers from several nearby factories had blocked the roads.
Law enforcers were working to remove them and restore normal traffic, he added.

item.title: Former DSCC mayor Sayeed Khokon arrested in Dhaka
item.description:

He was arrested around 7am on Tuesday.
According to a statement from the Special Response Battalion (SRB), a team of SRB-01 arrested him from House 13 on Road 9 in Baridhara.
Following his arrest, Sayeed Khokon was placed in the custody of Gulshan police station.

item.title: Nahid condemns attack on expatriate Bangladeshis, students in London
item.description:
National Citizen Party (NCP) Convener and opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam has accused activists of the Awami League, whose activities are currently banned, of attacking expatriate Bangladeshis and students from various universities after a reception held in London, saying several people were injured.
In a Facebook post on Tuesday, Nahid blamed what he described as “fugitive and extremist activists of the Awami League” for the attack and strongly condemned the incident.
In his post, Nahid said expatriate Bangladeshis from different parts of the UK, students from various universities, community leaders and leaders of the 11-party alliance attended the reception in London. He expressed deep gratitude and appreciation for their large turnout.
He alleged that after the event, fugitive activists of the Awami League attacked ordinary expatriate Bangladeshis and university students who had attended the program, leaving several people injured. He also wished the injured a speedy recovery.
Nahid said representatives of international human rights organisations and journalists from various media outlets were present at the event and witnessed the attack and violence firsthand. He expressed hope that the incident would draw international attention based on their firsthand accounts and collected information.
In his Facebook post, he said the people of Bangladesh had witnessed the Awami League's history of political violence, repression and destruction of democratic institutions.
He said individuals linked to the political force, which was ousted from power through the July uprising, were now attempting to suppress dissent through violence and intimidation even on foreign soil.
Such actions, he said, raised concerns not only about the safety of expatriate Bangladeshis but also about the democratic environment and political freedom.
“There is no right to use the opportunities of democracy to perpetrate anti-democratic violence,” he said.
Nahid added that using political asylum, freedom of expression and the right to assembly in a democratic country like the UK as tools for violence and intimidation was unacceptable.
He called on the UK government to ensure a prompt, impartial and effective investigation into the incident.
He also demanded legal action against those involved in the attack and effective measures to prevent acts of terrorism and violence carried out under the cover of the UK's democratic space.

item.title: Awami League, NCP activists clash in London, four injured
item.description:
At least four people were injured in clashes between activists of the Awami League, whose activities are currently banned and the National Citizen Party (NCP) on a road behind London's Mayfair Hall following a reception for NCP Convener and opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam on Monday night.
The injured were admitted to local hospitals, while London police baton-charged protesters several times to bring the situation under control.
Members of the British-Bangladeshi community and prominent figures expressed strong dismay over the incident, saying that bringing political rivalries from Bangladesh to London was deeply embarrassing for the entire community.
The reception was organised at Mayfair Hall in central London by members of the British-Bangladeshi community as part of Nahid Islam's week-long visit to the UK.
During the event, activists of the Awami League and its affiliated organisations gathered outside the venue.
According to eyewitnesses and organisers, Awami League supporters threw eggs and water bottles at guests arriving at the event and confronted them outside the hall.
After the program ended, activists of the Awami League and the NCP engaged in chasing and counter-chasing, followed by around 20 minutes of scuffles on the road behind the hall.
Saiful Islam, Prothom Alo's UK correspondent who was present at the venue, said Nahid Islam entered Mayfair Hall at around 3pm, more than three hours ahead of the scheduled time. He was therefore able to enter before the protesters gathered.
Nahid avoided any direct confrontation as he left the venue through a back entrance instead of the main gate after the event.
The incident sparked strong reactions among British-Bangladeshi residents, civil society representatives and guests attending the programme.
Cultural organiser Mahbubur Rahman Shiblu said the long-standing culture of such disruptive behaviour must end so that community events abroad are not overshadowed by street violence.

item.title: Titumir: Every taka borrowed must deliver maximum economic, social benefits
item.description:
Prime Minister's Adviser on Finance and Planning Dr Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir today said the government is focusing not on how much it borrows, but on ensuring that every unit of public resources generates the maximum possible economic and social benefits.
"We are not debating whether we should borrow less or borrow more. Rather, our focus is on how to borrow better, invest better and ensure the highest economic and social returns from every unit of public resources, while remaining accountable to the people," he said.
He was speaking as the chief guest at the concluding session of the two-day 'International Debt Conference Bangladesh 2026' in Cox's Bazar.
Describing borrowing as a means rather than an end to development, Dr Titumir said borrowed funds should be invested in sectors that enhance productivity, improve infrastructure, create employment opportunities and develop human resources.
He stressed that the economic and social returns from borrowing must be commensurate with the liabilities passed on to future generations.
Highlighting the challenging economic circumstances facing Bangladesh, the adviser said geopolitical conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East had increased the country's energy import expenditure by $4.2 billion.
"This additional expenditure was neither our choice nor something we could avoid," he said.
Referring to the human impact of the economic pressures, he said around eight million Bangladeshis had fallen below the poverty line again amid inflation and economic disruptions.
Many people who had worked hard to escape poverty were pushed back into it, he said, adding that these were not merely figures in statistical records but real hardships affecting people's lives.
Dr Titumir said the figures were not intended to blame anyone but to explain the circumstances in which the present government began its journey.
Understanding the starting point, he added, was essential to properly assess progress and the challenges ahead.
Describing the country's debt situation, he said Bangladesh's public debt had exceeded Tk18.9 trillion, equivalent to around 36% of GDP. Total external debt of the public and private sectors stood at more than $104 billion.
The government was spending over Tk1 trillion annually on interest payments alone. In addition, he said, Tk 56,750 crore had previously been borrowed from Bangladesh Bank to finance the budget deficit.
Emphasising the need for prudent debt management, he said the government must take all existing liabilities and associated risks into account while formulating its borrowing strategy.
As grace periods on previously contracted external loans were coming to an end, debt repayment pressures would increase in the coming years, he noted.
Bangladesh repaid $4.49 billion in principal and interest on external loans in the fiscal year 2025-26, and the annual repayment amount could rise to $7.6 billion by FY2030, he said.
Therefore, he stressed, decisions on new borrowing must carefully consider interest rates, maturity periods, repayment schedules, currency composition and exchange-rate risks.
Identifying national ownership and credibility as two fundamental pillars of debt management, Dr Titumir said borrowing decisions must be aligned with the country's development priorities and economic realities.
Transparency regarding debt data, expenditure and risks, alongside accountability to the public, was directly linked to the credibility of government debt management, he added.
The adviser also identified increased revenue mobilisation as a key condition for sustainable debt management.
Noting that Bangladesh's tax-to-GDP ratio remained low, he said the government aimed to increase the revenue-to-GDP ratio by two percentage points over the next five years.
The target would be pursued through expanding the tax base, digitalising tax administration and bringing more economic activities into the formal sector, he said. Higher revenue collection would help maintain a balance between development expenditure and debt servicing.
Highlighting the government's initiatives, Dr Titumir said the present government had stopped borrowing from Bangladesh Bank to finance the budget deficit.
As a result, pressure on money supply had eased and inflation had started declining from around 10%. Foreign exchange reserves had also risen above $30 billion, he said.
He further said the interest rate on 91-day Treasury bills had declined from around 12% to nearly 8%. The government had also taken initiatives to mobilise financing through long-term bonds and Sukuk.
Emphasising the need to develop the domestic capital market as a source of long-term financing, he said Bangladesh must maintain a balanced mix of domestic and external borrowing, short-term and long-term financing, and concessional and market-based loans.
He also stressed the importance of exploring alternative financing mechanisms, including private investment, public-private partnerships (PPPs), blended finance and credit guarantees.
Regarding the use of new financial instruments, including sovereign Sukuk, the adviser said Bangladesh's local-currency government securities had been included in JP Morgan's GBI-EM index.
He described the inclusion as an important milestone for the country's domestic currency bond market.
Alongside strengthening the capacity of the domestic bond market for long-term financing, Bangladesh also had opportunities to raise funds from international capital markets in a responsible and sustainable manner, he added.
Dr Titumir underscored the need for institutional reforms in debt management, including the establishment of a dedicated debt management office, enactment of a Public Debt Act and strengthening analytical capacity for debt data and risk assessment.
Regular publication of debt information, a medium-term debt strategy, an annual borrowing plan and transparent disclosure of contingent liabilities arising from government guarantees would help identify fiscal risks in advance, he said.
Outlining the government's strategy for economic transformation, he identified three phases:
He said the country aimed to move forward through economic recovery, restoration of institutional capacity and structural reconstruction.
Referring to Bangladesh's aspiration to become a US$1 trillion economy by 2034, he identified production, industrialisation, export capacity and employment generation as the key drivers of economic transformation.
Highlighting the economic importance of social protection programmes, the adviser said initiatives such as the Family Card and Farmer Card would contribute to improving living standards, reducing poverty and expanding economic inclusion.
These programmes were not merely forms of assistance but strategic investments in human development and long-term economic capacity, he said.
He also noted that the World Bank and development partners viewed these initiatives as part of the government's planned and financially responsible strategy.
Dr Titumir said the success of debt management should not be measured merely by how much money a country borrowed or repaid.
Rather, the real measure of success would be the extent to which borrowed funds transformed the economy and people's lives and generated economic and social benefits for future generations, he added.
The two-day conference, held on November 15-16, discussed sustainable sovereign debt management, borrowing costs and risks, international bond markets, the IMF's debt sustainability assessment framework, development of domestic bond markets and alternative sources of financing.
Around 100 delegates from nearly 30 countries, including Bangladesh, participated in the conference jointly organised by the Finance Division and the Asian Development Bank (ADB).
Participants included officials from the Finance Ministry and Bangladesh Bank, debt management experts from different countries, and representatives of the World Bank, IMF and ADB.
Representatives from the debt management offices of Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Indonesia and Malaysia also attended the conference.

National University VC freed after 12-hour standoff; offices closed for three days
item.description:
National University Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr ASM Amanullah was freed after being confined to his office for around 12 hours amid a protest by 988 reinstated staff members over their demands.
He was able to leave his office at around 11:30pm on Monday after the staff members staged a day-long siege and sit-in, pressing for resolution of issues related to seniority, promotions and outstanding salaries and allowances.
Meanwhile, the university authorities have decided to keep all university offices closed for three days, from Tuesday to Thursday, to address the situation.
The decision was taken at an emergency meeting of the university’s Syndicate on Monday night. It was announced in a press release signed by Taiyeba Tasneem Siraj, acting director of the National University’s Public Relations Department.
According to the release, all university offices will remain closed from November 17 to 19. However, essential services, the Office of the Controller of Examinations and activities related to the Principals' Conference will remain operational.
The 988 reinstated staff members had been protesting for the second consecutive day, demanding resolution of issues including seniority, promotions and payment of outstanding salaries and allowances.
They began surrounding the vice-chancellor’s office at the university’s main campus in Gazipur on Monday morning. At one point, they locked the main gate, effectively bringing the campus to a standstill and preventing the vice-chancellor from leaving his office.
The protesters said they had been reinstated following a court order but had continued to face discrimination over seniority, promotions and salary and allowance payments. They also alleged that they were being denied the benefits of the current pay scale.
They further claimed that while the university continued to recruit new staff and spend money in other areas, no effective steps had been taken to settle their outstanding dues.
On Sunday, the staff members had also surrounded the vice-chancellor’s office to submit a memorandum outlining their demands.
Amid the impasse, an emergency Syndicate meeting was convened at 10pm on Monday at the vice-chancellor’s office on the university’s main campus. The meeting was chaired by Professor Amanullah, and the decision to close university offices for three days was taken there.
In a Facebook post around 8pm on Monday, the vice-chancellor alleged that the 988 reinstated officers and employees had confined him for nine hours.
“My administration will not take any action that goes against the interests of the National University. I have acted in accordance with the court's verdict; for the rest, I will follow the government's directives. I have never bowed to pressure in the past, and I will not do so now,” he wrote.
He also said the university needed reform and that he had taken several initiatives towards that goal, but such efforts could not succeed if he was prevented from working.
Describing the blockade and confinement as futile, he wrote: “You have held me confined for nine hours; even if you were to keep me confined for 90 hours, it would achieve nothing.”
The officers and employees concerned were appointed to various positions between November 17, 2003, and August 31, 2004, but were dismissed from service in 2012, leading to a prolonged legal battle.
On May 27, 2025, a seven-member bench of the Appellate Division ordered the reinstatement of the surviving dismissed staff members. The court directed that their period of dismissal be treated as “extraordinary leave” and that their seniority be preserved.
However, the university authorities were tasked with determining matters relating to salaries, allowances and other benefits, taking humanitarian and practical considerations into account.
Following the implementation of the court verdict, the 988 reinstated staff members began protesting for recognition of their seniority, promotions and payment of outstanding salaries and allowances. The latest demonstration brought normal activities on the university’s main campus to a halt, prompting the authorities to call an emergency Syndicate meeting and announce the three-day office closure.

item.title: Holders India, first-time finalists Pakistan face off in SAFF final
item.description:
Defending champions India will take on first-time finalists Pakistan in the SAFF Championship 2026 final at the National Stadium in Dhaka on Tuesday.
India are aiming to secure a record-extending 10th title and become the first team to win three consecutive editions of the regional competition. Pakistan, meanwhile, will be looking to lift their maiden SAFF Championship trophy in their first-ever final appearance.
Scheduled to kick off at 8pm, the final promises to be a fascinating contest between the traditional rivals, with India seeking to extend their dominance and Pakistan hoping to script a historic triumph.
India are the most successful team in SAFF Championship history, having lifted the trophy in 1993, 1997, 1999, 2005, 2009, 2011, 2015, 2021 and 2023.
Despite their dominance, India have never won the championship in three consecutive editions. A victory on Tuesday would see them achieve that milestone while further extending their record.
Head coach Naushad Moosa's young side booked their place in the final with a 2-1 victory over Bhutan in the first semifinal. PV Vishnu and captain Chinglensana Singh Konsham scored in the first half to give India a two-goal cushion before Kinzang Tashi Tobden pulled one back shortly after the break.
Pakistan, meanwhile, made history by defeating hosts Bangladesh 1-0 in the other semifinal. Abdul Samad Arshad broke the deadlock with a late winner in the 86th minute to send Pakistan into their maiden SAFF final.
The victory marked another significant milestone in a remarkable year for Pakistan football, as they now stand just one win away from claiming their first regional title.
The traditional rivals have already met once in this edition, with India securing a 3-2 victory in their opening Group B encounter on November 5. India established a commanding 3-0 lead through a brace from Suhail Ahmad Bhat and a goal from Manglenthang Kipgen before Pakistan scored twice in stoppage time to make the contest considerably closer.
Pakistan's disciplined defensive display against Bangladesh, despite facing sustained pressure from the hosts, will provide them with confidence heading into the title-deciding encounter.

item.title: Ackerman leads South Africa fightback after Hasan strikes
item.description:
Marques Ackerman struck his maiden Test century to lead South Africa's fightback against Bangladesh, despite Hasan Mahmud's impressive bowling, as the hosts reached 287-4 at stumps on Day 2 of the first Test at the Wanderers Stadium in Johannesburg today.
Ackerman made 157 off 164, smashing 21 fours and one six while Zubayr Hamza scored 83, helping South Africa recover from an early setback and cut Bangladesh's first-innings lead to 113 runs. The hosts had resumed their reply after Bangladesh were bowled out for 400.
Captain Temba Bavuma was unbeaten on 19, with Ryan Rickelton on 7 at the close.
The highlight of South Africa's innings was a commanding 202-run second-wicket partnership between Ackerman and Hamza, who steadied the innings after Hasan removed Aiden Markram in the second over.
Markram, who made 5, tentatively edged a scrambled-seam delivery from Hasan.
Ackerman and Hamza weathered some testing spells, remaining unbeaten throughout the second session despite sustained pressure from Hasan and Taskin Ahmed.
Taskin came close to dismissing Hamza, who was trapped leg-before, but the bowler had overstepped and the delivery was called a no-ball.
Ackerman looked increasingly assured and brought up his third consecutive fifty off 68 balls, whipping Mehidy Hasan Miraz through deep midwicket for four.
Hamza, after some early struggles, also settled into his innings, reaching his half-century off 82 balls with a single off Mehidy.
With his frontline bowlers struggling to break the partnership, Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto turned to Mominul Haque, and the move paid off.
Mominul ended Hamza's resistance with his left-arm spin, dismissing him for 83 off 129 balls, an innings featuring 12 boundaries.
Ackerman continued to dominate, reaching his maiden Test century off 125 balls with a single off Taskin. He then accelerated, putting Bangladesh's bowlers under further pressure before Hasan ended his innings at 157, having him caught by Taskin at backward square leg.
The dismissal also broke a 61-run partnership between Ackerman and Bavuma. Hasan struck again soon afterwards, removing Matthew Breetzke for 2 to prevent South Africa from taking complete control of the contest.
He also could have dismissed Ryan Rickelton, who edged a delivery behind, but Liton Das dropped the catch.
Earlier, Bangladesh resumed the day at 327-6 but managed only 73 more runs before being bowled out for 400.
Liton Das, who began the day on 89, completed his eighth Test century off 154 balls, pulling Marco Jansen to the fine-leg boundary.
Dane Paterson eventually dismissed Liton for 120 off 154 balls, an innings featuring 14 fours and a six. He became the second Bangladesh batter to score a century in the innings, following Towhid Hridoy's 137.
It was the first time two Bangladesh batters had scored centuries in the same Test innings against South Africa. Their efforts propelled Bangladesh to 400, their highest Test total on South African soil.
Paterson then cleaned up the tail, taking all four remaining wickets in the morning session to finish with figures of 4-92.

item.title: Awami League back on Gopalganj streets despite security clampdown
item.description:
Leaders and activists of the activities-banned Awami League reopened their party office and the mausoleum of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in Tungipara on Monday, pledging to bring former prime minister Sheikh Hasina back to Bangladesh, even as security forces intensified operations across Gopalganj following Sunday's widespread violence and vandalism.
The renewed political mobilisation came as normal life gradually resumed in the district town under heavy security, with Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel patrolling in armoured vehicles and police stationed at key roads and government installations.
Around 11am, Awami League and Chhatra League activists gathered in Tungipara and marched to the local party office, where they hoisted the national flag and the party flag while singing the national anthem.
The procession, reportedly led by Tungipara municipal Chhatra League president Sheikh Ifti Zaman Pallab, subsequently entered Bangabandhu's mausoleum complex after opening three gates.
Participants took an oath to continue their movement until Sheikh Hasina returned to Bangladesh.
"We have come together with the singular goal of bringing former prime minister Sheikh Hasina back to the country," Pallab said.
He declared that the party office would again serve as a gathering place for activists and that a wider movement would be launched from Tungipara.
Speaking at a press briefing near the old launch terminal in Gopalganj town around 5:15pm, Dhaka Range DIG Md Mostafizur Rahman said approximately 2,000 security personnel had been deployed to maintain law and order.
The deployment included police, 10 platoons of BGB and personnel from the Special Reserve Battalion, Armed Police Battalion and Ansar.
He said several suspects had been arrested during operations following Sunday's violence but did not disclose the number.
No case had yet been filed in connection with the incidents, he added.
Checkposts have been established at entry points from neighbouring districts to prevent outsiders from entering Gopalganj to create disturbances.
Responding to questions about the reopening of the Awami League office and mausoleum, the DIG warned that police would take legal action against any unlawful activity.
The latest developments followed the transfer of Gopalganj Deputy Commissioner Md Arif-uz-Zaman and Superintendent of Police Md Habibullah.
Three officers-in-charge were also transferred to Kishoreganj district: Md Ayub Ali of Tungipara police station, Riad Mahmud of Kotalipara and Mahfuzur Rahman of Kashiani.
The transfers were announced in an order signed by Dhaka Range DIG Mostafizur Rahman on Sunday.
However, the DIG rejected suggestions that the SP had been withdrawn as a disciplinary measure, describing the transfer as part of the police's regular administrative process.
On Sunday, Awami League and affiliated activists staged armed processions across Gopalganj, vandalised public property and reportedly attacked political opponents' establishments.
The incidents included attacks on BNP leaders' homes, damage to police property and the burning of a Grameen Bank branch, according to local accounts.
Despite the unrest, residents began returning to their daily activities on Monday. Shops reopened, educational institutions resumed classes and public transport returned to the streets.
However, fear persisted among residents following the violence.

Doctors may receive Tk1,861cr a year in commissions for test referrals
item.description:
Doctors in Bangladesh receive commissions ranging from 20% to 50% of the fees for the respective tests by advising patients to undergo tests at various diagnostic centres, a study by Bangladesh Health Watch (BHW) has found.
According to the study’s calculations, transactions worth approximately Tk1,861 crore may take place annually in the country’s major diagnostic centres in the form of such commissions.
The report noted, however, that this figure needs to be independently verified.
The study also revealed widespread irregularities in the health sector, including doctors’ absence from government hospitals and irregularities in the purchase of medical equipment. Nearly 40% of doctors at government hospitals were not found at their workplaces during surprise inspections. The study also found financial losses of Tk459 crore in purchases by the Central Medical Stores Depot (CMSD) and medical equipment worth Tk283 crore lying unused. There were instances of equipment being purchased at prices 18 times higher than its market value.
These findings were presented on Sunday at the publication ceremony of BHW’s 2025-26 biennial report at the International Mother Language Institute in Dhaka. The 191-page report contains 11 chapters written by 17 researchers. It was edited by BHW Convener Dr Ahmed Mustaque Raza Chowdhury and Dr Shams El Arifeen, Emeritus Scientist at the International Centre for Diarrhoeal Disease Research, Bangladesh (icddr,b). The Embassy of Sweden and the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida) assisted in preparing the report.
Speaking at the ceremony, Dr Shams El Arifeen said weak governance, excessive decision-making powers without accountability, failure to control conflicts of interest, and lack of coordination in monitoring are mainly responsible for corruption in the health sector. The institutional tendency to accept irregularities as normal also plays a role in sustaining it, he said.
He said corruption cannot be eliminated through law enforcement alone, and that integrity and ethics must be developed as inseparable parts of institutional culture.
State Minister for Health MA Muhith said bringing those involved in corruption to justice alone would not solve the problem, and that necessary reforms must be made to the overall structure of the health sector. Alongside financial irregularities and manipulation of tenders, he said, influencing policies and strategies in the interests of a particular group also falls under corruption.
The report highlighted various irregularities and harassment faced by patients seeking treatment at government hospitals. These include being forced to obtain services through brokers, illegal payments for bed allocation and hospital discharge, and referrals to private clinics and diagnostic centres.
In one such incident, a hospital ward boy took Tk5,000 from an elderly patient by promising to arrange a date for surgery, though there were no arrangements for surgery in the relevant ward. Later, instead of disciplinary action being taken against the employee, he was transferred to another place.
The absence of doctors from government hospitals and health centres was identified as one of the biggest challenges in healthcare services. Besides the surprise inspections that found nearly 40% of doctors absent, another study found that absence rates at several health centres in remote areas exceeded 70%.
The report also highlighted the issue of receiving government salaries and allowances without performing duties. Researchers further identified political influence and weaknesses in the paper-based management system in the recruitment, transfer and promotion of more than 180,000 employees in the health sector. As an example, the report mentioned the cancellation of the recruitment of 2,839 health workers in 2021.
BHW also raised questions about the independence and accountability of regulatory institutions in the health sector. Of approximately 90 members of the Bangladesh Medical and Dental Council (BMDC), 70 are associated with the government. None of the six regulatory bodies reviewed has effective representation of patients or the general public.
The report found evidence of delays in resolving allegations of medical negligence. From 2010 to May 2025, a total of 172 complaints were submitted to the BMDC. Of these, 79 are still awaiting resolution, and disciplinary action has been taken in only 29 cases.
The report further stated that although the number of medical colleges has increased rapidly, from 62 in 2010 to 118 in 2022-23, sufficient measures have not been developed to ensure the quality of medical education. Quality control and monitoring systems have not improved accordingly.
To reduce corruption and irregularities, BHW has recommended making all information on government procurement publicly available and ensuring accountability at every stage, from the purchase of medical equipment to its use. It has also stressed the protection of those who disclose information about corruption.
To ensure the independence of regulatory bodies, the organisation has proposed preventing ministers, secretaries and members of parliament from becoming heads of these institutions. It has also recommended ensuring representation of patients and the general public in regulatory bodies, and establishing an independent mechanism for appeals against their decisions.

item.title: Bangladesh’s largest solar power plant expected to begin operations in June 2028
item.description:
Electricity Generation Bangladesh (EGB) is constructing the country's largest solar power plant with a capacity of 220 megawatts (MW) in Sonagazi, Feni, at an estimated cost of Tk 1,888.10 crore, with plans to complete the project by June 30, 2028.
State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Anindya Islam Amit inaugurated a start-up workshop on the project on Monday.
Speaking at the event, the state minister said the government aims to meet 20 percent of the country’s electricity demand from renewable energy sources by 2030. "Our target is to generate 10,000 megawatts of electricity from renewable sources by 2030. The government has formulated supportive policies in this regard," he said, adding that the Sonagazi 220MW solar project will play an important role in achieving that goal.
According to a press release, the project is being implemented under joint financing from the Bangladesh government, the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB), and EGB's own funds. A financing agreement between the Economic Relations Division (ERD) and IsDB was signed on August 3.
Once operational, the plant is expected to supply around 441.18 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of electricity annually to the national grid starting in June 2028, contributing significantly to the government's target of generating 10,000MW from solar energy by 2030.
Under the project, around 469,560 solar photovoltaic (PV) modules, 26 inverters, and two substations will be installed. There are also plans to introduce an agrivoltaic concept to allow agricultural activities and livestock rearing alongside solar power generation on the same land.
Additionally, the project includes initiatives to provide skill development training for about 1,000 local unemployed youths and women, set up computer labs, and install rooftop solar panels at local educational institutions.
Meanwhile, the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) approved a project on September 29 to acquire 386 acres of land for building another 130MW solar power plant in Sonagazi. Alongside this, there is a plan to construct a 150MW floating solar power plant at Muchapur. Once implemented, these initiatives could transform the area into a major solar power hub with a combined capacity of around 600MW.
EGB believes the project is not merely an initiative to boost electricity generation, but will also play a vital role in promoting clean energy, environmental protection, local employment, and sustainable socio-economic development.
Power Division Secretary Mirana Mahrook, IsDB Dhaka Regional Hub Resident Head Ali M. Khan, Operational Team Leader Nasser Mohammed Yakubu, EGB Chairman K. M. Ali Reza, Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB) Chairman Md. Rezaul Karim, and EGB Managing Director A K M Manjur Kadir, among other officials, attended the workshop.

item.title: Rajshahi farmers reap bumper Aman harvest, but low prices sour the mood
item.description:
Farmers in Rajshahi are enjoying a bumper Aman harvest this season, with yields reaching 17–20 maunds per bigha in some areas thanks to favourable weather. However, their joy is being dampened by low market prices, with paddy selling for just Tk1,200 per maund.
Rising costs of fertiliser, pesticides, diesel and labour have pushed up production expenses, leaving farmers worried about their returns. They say paddy should fetch at least Tk1,400–1,500 per maund to cover costs and ensure a reasonable profit.
Harvesting of early-maturing transplanted Aman varieties began in different parts of the district in early November. The Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE) expects harvesting to gain pace over the next one to two weeks.
During a visit to the Teghor, Bagsara and Paikpara fields in Nawhata municipality of Paba upazila on Monday morning, vast stretches of farmland were seen covered with ripe and partially ripe golden paddy. Farmers were busy harvesting, bundling and threshing the crop, while their families were preparing to bring the harvest home.
Local farmers said early-maturing BRRI-103 and BINA-17 varieties had produced good yields this year. Some have already completed harvesting and sold their produce. However, higher production costs have raised concerns about profitability. Many are preparing their fields for potatoes, winter vegetables and pulses after harvesting Aman.
Mamun Rashid of Teghor village cultivated BRRI-103 Aman on three bighas, harvesting 20 maunds per bigha.
He said land preparation, planting and fertiliser application cost Tk7,000 per bigha, while harvesting, threshing, transportation and labour expenses added another Tk7,000. This brought the total production cost to Tk14,000 per bigha on his own land. Cultivation on leased or sharecropped land requires an additional Tk5,000.
Mamun said he sold 20 maunds of paddy at Nawhata market on Sunday for Tk1,200 per maund, earning Tk24,000. After deducting production costs, his return from paddy was Tk10,000 per bigha.
He also harvested around 21 bundles of straw per bigha, selling each for Tk250 and earning another Tk5,250. Including straw sales, his surplus came to around Tk15,250 per bigha.
He is now preparing the land for potato cultivation.
Munzur Rahman, a farmer from Bagsara Beel, cultivated BINA-17 Aman on 10 bighas at a production cost of Tk17,000 per bigha. His average yield was 18 maunds.
He recently sold 20 maunds at Tk1,200 each but has kept the remaining paddy in the hope of better prices. After accounting for all expenses and income from straw sales, he said he made a profit of around Tk10,000 per bigha.
Shahidul Islam of Paikpara, who cultivated BRRI-51 Aman on three bighas of leased land, expects to begin harvesting next week.
He said fertiliser, pesticide and diesel prices, as well as labour wages, had increased compared with last year.
"At Tk1,200 per maund, farmers cannot make a reasonable profit. The price needs to be at least Tk1,500 to make cultivation worthwhile," he said.
Yusuf Ali, another farmer from Paba, cultivated BRRI-10 Aman on five bighas of sharecropped land. He has already harvested two bighas, with an average yield of 18 maunds per bigha.
He said the harvest had been good and the crop had been brought in on time, but sharecroppers would not benefit unless they received a fair price.
According to the Rajshahi DAE, the cultivation target for transplanted Aman this season was 83,600 hectares. Farmers have cultivated 83,670 hectares, exceeding the target by 70 hectares.
The district's total production target has been set at 314,336 tonnes. So far, harvesting has been completed on 12,423 hectares, while the targeted average yield is 17–20 maunds per bigha.
Godagari leads the district in Aman cultivation, with 23,762 hectares, followed by Tanore with 22,071 hectares, Paba with 9,140 hectares, Durgapur with 5,645 hectares, Charghat with 5,450 hectares, Mohanpur with 4,100 hectares, Bagmara with 3,725 hectares and Bagha with 2,352 hectares.
Bagha Upazila Agriculture Officer MA Mannan said Aman had been cultivated on 2,352 hectares in the upazila this season, with an average yield of around 20 maunds per bigha.
Rajshahi DAE Deputy Director Mostafa Kamal Hossain said harvesting had been completed on 12,423 hectares and full-scale harvesting was expected to begin within the next one to two weeks.
He attributed the good yield to favourable weather and a lower incidence of pests and diseases.
He added that farmers were preparing to cultivate potatoes, mustard, maize, wheat and winter vegetables on the same land after harvesting early Aman, creating opportunities for multiple cropping.
The government has decided to procure paddy at fair prices to support farmers, he said, adding that the agriculture department would also monitor the market to help ensure farmers receive reasonable prices.

item.title: Dhaka to host 51st ICQCC from November 18
item.description:
The 51st International Convention on Quality Control Circles (ICQCC-2026) will be held in Dhaka from November 18 to 20 under the theme “QCC for Sustainable Development.”
The Bangladesh Society for Total Quality Management (BSTQM) and the University of Asia Pacific (UAP) are jointly organizing the convention. Around 8,000 members of approximately 800 Quality Control Circle (QCC) teams from 16 countries and regions are expected to participate.
Details of the convention were shared at a press conference held at Pan Pacific Sonargaon Dhaka on Sunday. Those present included BSTQM President and ICQCC-2026 Convener A K M Shamsul Huda, BSTQM Adviser Engr. A M M Khairul Bashar, UAP Registrar Brig Gen (Retd) Prof Dr A K M Nazrul Islam, BSTQM Secretary General M M Kabir, and ICQCC-2026 Technical and Evaluation Committee Member Md Rokibul Islam, along with representatives of BSTQM and UAP and members of the media.
Of the participating teams, 141 will present onsite and 652 online. The main presentation sessions will be held at UAP on November 19 and 20, where teams will showcase workplace improvement projects focusing on productivity, quality enhancement, cost reduction and problem-solving.
Nearly 100 local and international judges will evaluate the presentations.
Participating countries and regions include Japan, China, India, South Korea, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Sri Lanka, the Philippines, Taiwan, Namibia, Zambia, Mozambique and Mauritius, along with Bangladesh.
ICQCC is coordinated internationally by the Union of Japanese Scientists and Engineers (JUSE) of Japan and is known as the “Quality Olympics.” It is one of the world's largest annual platforms for promoting QCC and Total Quality Management (TQM).
Bangladesh is hosting the convention for the third time.
The convention will conclude on November 20 with the announcement of results, a prize-giving ceremony and the formal handover of the ICQCC flag to the Philippines, host of the next convention.

item.title: Garment factories in Savar, Ashulia return to normal operations
item.description:
Garment factories in Savar and Ashulia have maintained normal production following several days of tension, with most workers returning to work peacefully on Monday morning.
A visit to different industrial areas in the morning found workers entering factories within their scheduled hours.
However, law enforcement agencies remained on alert to prevent any untoward incidents. Additional police and members of other forces were deployed at key points and in front of factories.
Despite the overall improvement, production remained suspended at several factories in Ashulia.
Industrial police said more than 30 factories across the industrial zone remained closed due to labour unrest, while workers at two factories were observing work stoppages. All other factories remained open.
Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan, superintendent of police of Industrial Police-1, said the situation in Savar, Ashulia and Dhamrai under his jurisdiction was normal, with operations running smoothly.
"Factory owners have kept around 30 factories closed for various reasons. Operations have been normal everywhere since morning. Workers at only two factories are observing work stoppages. No disorder has been reported elsewhere," he said.
He said the industrial zone has around 800 garment factories, of which approximately 30 remain closed.
Of these, 27 factories have been closed under Section 13(1) of the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006, four are observing general holidays, and nine have been declared closed indefinitely. Workers at two factories joined work but later stopped working, he added.
He said factory owners and other stakeholders all want stability in the garment sector.
Khairul Mamun Mintu, legal affairs secretary of the Bangladesh Garment and Sweater Workers Trade Union Centre, said the situation had remained normal since morning.
"Some factories that were previously closed have reopened. Workers have joined work, and the situation remains normal so far. In a small number of factories where workers had joined but were not working, holidays have been declared under Section 13(1) of the Labour Act, following the 'no work, no pay' principle. Apart from these, the situation across the industrial zone is normal," he said.

item.title: Iran rules out UN inspections of damaged nuclear sites until war ends
item.description:
Iran will not let UN inspectors visit its damaged nuclear facilities until the Middle East war has ended and the United States meets its conditions, a senior Iranian official said.
The remarks came days after the International Atomic Energy Agency urged Tehran to take steps towards resuming inspections, which have been suspended since last year’s 12-day war with Israel, when the US also struck Iranian nuclear sites.
“We will not grant the IAEA access to the facilities until Iran’s conditions are met and the war has permanently ended,” Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said in a televised interview late Sunday.
Iranian nuclear facilities were hit again during the Middle East war which broke out on February 28 when US-Israeli strikes killed Iran’s supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
IAEA inspectors visited Iran’s Bushehr nuclear power plant in September but have not gained access to other bombed sites including Natanz, Fordow and Isfahan.
Gharibabadi said the agency’s request to inspect damaged facilities was “likely aimed at assessing the effectiveness of American weaponry.”
Efforts to end the Middle East war have made little headway. Tehran is demanding that Washington unfreeze Iranian assets and lift sanctions, among other conditions, in exchange for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, the vital energy shipping route it has blockaded during the conflict.
Iranian officials have said talks on Iran’s nuclear program would come at a later stage.
Earlier this month, the US military announced a $20 million reward for information on Iran’s nuclear program, a move Tehran called “repugnant.”

item.title: Bangladesh exports fruits worth $126.35m in FY26
item.description:
Bangladesh exported fruits worth $126.35 million in FY26, Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir told the parliament on Sunday.
“Bangladesh exports fruits to various international markets, including the United Arab Emirates, Austria, Australia, Bahrain, Canada, China, India, Japan, Malaysia, Saudi Arabia, the United Kingdom and the United States,” he said.
The minister said this while responding to a starred question from treasury bench member Md. Sadique Reaz (Dinajpur-2) during the day’s question-answer session in the House today with Deputy Speaker Barrister Kayser Kamal in the chair.
The minister said Bangladesh currently exports fruits to various countries and territories, including Austria, Bahrain, Germany, Denmark, France, Greece, Hong Kong, Ireland, Italy, Kuwait, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Oman, Poland, Portugal, Qatar, Sweden, Singapore and Vietnam.
Muktadir outlined several initiatives undertaken by the Export Promotion Bureau (EPB) to expand exports of mangoes and other agricultural products.
He said the EPB organized a seminar titled “Export Opportunities and Diversification of Mango and Mango Products” in Chapainawabganj on October 19, 2023, to explore export potential, market expansion and diversification of mango and mango-based products.
The EPB also held a view exchange meeting with local mango growers, exporters and other stakeholders in Chapainawabganj on May 20, 2025, in presence of its vice-chairman, he added.
The minister said the EPB had provided comprehensive assistance to exporters in completing the General Administration of Customs of China (GACC) registration process to expand agricultural exports, particularly mango shipments, to China.
“Meridian Agro Industries Ltd. of Chattogram has secured GACC registration with the overall support of the Export Promotion Bureau,” he said.
He added that the EPB had also processed questionnaires submitted by Safe International Corporation and MTB Agro and Garden and forwarded them to the Commercial Counsellor at the Bangladesh Embassy in China on June 7, 2023.
Muktadir said the EPB vice-chairman inspected the Vapour Heat Treatment Plant in Gabtoli, Dhaka, on July 22, 2026, to assess the infrastructure and procedures required for agricultural exports.
An EPB meeting with all stakeholders was also held on August 10, 2026, to discuss exports of mangoes, jackfruits and other agricultural products to China and other international markets, GACC registration and ways to address existing barriers.
The minister said the EPB had taken initiatives to organize training programs involving the Department of Agricultural Extension, all stakeholders and exporters on GACC registration and registration procedures in other countries, phytosanitary requirements and export compliance.
The EPB also organized a training program for mango growers, farmers and stakeholders in Lama, Bandarban, on May 9, 2026.
The program covered mango production, disease and pest management, timely harvesting, grading and packaging, post-harvest management, vapour and hot water treatment, export procedures and marketing, he said.
The minister further said the EPB had undertaken a survey to assess the export potential of the country’s Geographical Indication (GI) products.
The survey will identify production capacity, product quality, international market demand, existing barriers, compliance requirements and potential export destinations for promising GI products. The EPB has finalised the terms of reference for appointing a survey firm, he added.
As part of efforts to promote and brand GI products and other promising agricultural goods in international markets, the EPB has included participation in six international trade fairs in its calendar for FY27.
The fairs include the 2026 Mekong-Lancang Fruits Festival in China’s Yunnan Province, the 22nd Malaysia International Halal Showcase (MIHAS) 2026, D-8 Halal Expo Indonesia 2026, Agro Food Jeddah 2026, the International Food and Drink Event and the International Halal Expo and World Halal Summit 2026.
The minister said these initiatives aimed to diversify agricultural exports, improve compliance with international standards and strengthen Bangladesh’s presence in global markets.

item.title: Pallabi child rape-murder: Swapna helped Sohel out of fear, prosecution tells HC
item.description:
The wife of Sohel Rana, who was sentenced to death for the rape and murder of an eight-year-old child Pallabi, was so afraid of her husband that she helped him in the killing, the prosecution told the High Court on Monday.
The submission came during the hearing on the death references and appeals filed by Sohel and his wife, Swapna Akter, before a High Court bench led by Justice Bhishmadev Chakrabortty.
The prosecution concluded its arguments on the day. Deputy Attorney General Barrister Mohammad Osman Chowdhury represented the state.
According to the case documents, the child's father lived with his family in a rented flat in Pallabi. He worked at a private office in Banani.
Sohel Rana and Swapna Akter lived in another flat in the same building. The child was a second-grade student at a local school.
On May 19, the child was raped and murdered. Sohel later escaped by cutting through the window grille of the room.
Police took Swapna into custody after receiving information through the national emergency helpline 999. Sohel was later arrested in front of Fatullah police station in Narayanganj.
The child's father filed a case with Pallabi police station over the incident. On May 21, Sohel gave a confessional statement before a court under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898. Both accused were subsequently sent to jail.
On May 25, the investigating officer, Sub-Inspector Ahiduzzaman of Pallabi police station, submitted a charge sheet against Sohel and Swapna. The case was sent to the tribunal for trial on the same day.
The trial began on June 1 with the framing of charges against the two accused. The following day, the prosecution presented 16 witnesses, completing the recording of testimony in a single day.
The accused were examined under Section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, on June 3.
On June 7, Judge Masrur Salequin of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children's Violence Suppression Tribunal sentenced both accused to death.
The tribunal also fined Sohel Tk5 lakh and Swapna Tk2 lakh, directing that the money be paid to the child's legal heirs.
The verdict was delivered just 19 days after the murder.
The death references containing the case records were subsequently sent to the High Court for confirmation of the sentences. Both convicts later filed jail appeals before the High Court.

item.title: Midland Bank holds 201st executive committee meeting
item.description:

item.title: BCIC chairman warns of strict action against fertilizer irregularities
item.description:
Bangladesh Chemical Industries Corporation (BCIC) Chairman Md Babul Mia has warned of strict action against anyone involved in irregularities or corruption in fertilizer distribution and storage in the northern region.
He has also assured farmers that the country has adequate fertilizer stocks and there is no actual shortage.
Babul Mia made the remarks at a meeting of the monitoring committee on fertilizer transportation, storage and stock management at Rangpur Circuit House on November 13, said a press release.
The meeting, organised by the Rangpur district administration, was chaired by Rangpur Deputy Commissioner Israt Jahan. It focused on the progress of the project to construct 34 buffer warehouses and the current fertilizer stock, transportation and storage situation in the region.
Earlier, on November 12 and 13, the BCIC chairman visited under-construction buffer warehouses in Thakurgaon, Panchagarh, Lalmonirhat and Rangpur to assess the project's progress and the overall fertilizer supply situation.
During the visits, he inspected construction work and reviewed fertilizer transportation, storage and stock management at the sites.
He instructed the contractors and officials concerned to maintain construction quality and complete the work within the stipulated timeframe.
He also stressed the need to maintain adequate stocks in line with farmers' demand and ensure close monitoring of transportation and distribution to keep fertilizer supplies uninterrupted.
Addressing the meeting, Babul Mia said the government was taking all necessary measures to strengthen fertilizer supply and storage facilities in the northern region.
He warned that anyone involved in fertilizer-related irregularities or corruption would be brought to justice.
He said misleading claims about an artificial fertilizer shortage, spread by unscrupulous quarters, were creating confusion among farmers.
To prevent rumours and ensure transparency, he urged district administrations and officials concerned to regularly monitor fertilizer stocks and distribution.
He also advised farmers not to panic or stockpile more fertilizer than they need.

item.title: BADC project targets higher pulse, oilseed production
item.description:
The Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) is implementing a project to boost domestic production of pulses and oilseeds, reduce import dependence and strengthen the country's food and nutritional security.
According to a press release, the country's annual demand for pulses is 2.5 million tonnes, while domestic production stands at only 937,000 tonnes. Similarly, annual demand for edible oil is 2.482 million tonnes, against domestic production of 1.064 million tonnes, according to the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE).
The shortfall forces Bangladesh to import substantial quantities of pulses and edible oil, putting pressure on foreign currency reserves.
Approved by the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (Ecnec) on December 8, 2024, the project, titled "Strengthening Sustainable Nutritional Security through the Production of Pulses and Oilseeds (Phase 2)," will run from July 2025 to June 2029.
The project aims to produce 18,000 tonnes of quality seeds and distribute them among farmers. Its activities cover 42 districts, two city corporations and 200 upazilas across eight divisions through three farms, three seed processing centres and 12 contract-farming zones.
Project estimates suggest that the targeted seed production will generate an additional 256,499 tonnes of agricultural produce worth Tk2,964 crore over the project's duration.
During the 2025-26 fiscal year, the project produced 3,723.112 tonnes of pulse and oilseed seeds through contract farming. These included lentil, mung bean, mustard, soybean, groundnut and sunflower seeds, which are being distributed for the 2026-27 cropping season.
Their use is expected to generate an additional 51,455 tonnes of crops worth Tk597.57 crore across approximately 606,360 acres.
The project, costing Tk265.78 crore, also includes training for 2,000 contract farmers in seed production, processing and storage.
Project Director Dr Md Shafiqul Islam is overseeing implementation, including field-level activities and seed production and distribution.
The initiative is expected to increase farmers' incomes, create rural employment and reduce the country's reliance on imported pulses and edible oil.

item.title: Govt plans to digitise all post offices by February 2028
item.description:
The government plans to transform all post offices across the country into digital service centres by February 2028 under two ongoing projects aimed at modernising postal services.
The initiatives will digitise the Postal Department’s financial services and introduce a national digital address database and route-mapping tool, the ‘Amar Dak’ app and the ‘Dak Bazar’ software.
Post, Telecommunications and Information Technology Minister Fakir Mahbub Anam disclosed the plans on Monday while responding to a question from Rajshahi-5 MP Professor Nazrul Islam during the question-and-answer session on the sixth day of the fourth session of parliament.
The minister said a technical project titled “Sustainable and Modernisation of Mail Processing and Logistics Services” is being implemented from September 2024 to March 2027 to modernise postal operations and improve efficiency.
Another project, titled “Expansion and Accessibility of Existing Postal Services at Citizens’ Doorsteps”, is being implemented from March 2026 to February 2028.
Under the first project, the Postal Department’s existing electronic money transfer system is being upgraded to make it more modern and user-friendly.
The second project will digitise postal services through a national digital address database and route-mapping tool, the ‘Amar Dak’ app and the ‘Postal Rural Trade and Commerce Model’, known as ‘Dak Bazar’.
Once the projects are completed, all post offices will be transformed into digital service centres, allowing people across the country, including those in rural areas, to access secure digital postal services, the minister said.
Meanwhile, the minister outlined measures to prevent customer harassment, fraud and scams involving ‘Nagad’, the Postal Department’s digital financial service.
He said steps were being taken in line with directives from Bangladesh Bank, law enforcement agencies and the Directorate of Posts. Nagad provides round-the-clock customer support through its call centre at 16167, he said.
Currently, Nagad services are available at 97 post offices, while customer support is provided through a total of 113 service centres, including additional counters. Efforts are underway to gradually expand the network.
The minister said customers were regularly advised through awareness messages to keep their personal identification numbers (PINs) and one-time passwords (OTPs) confidential.
Suspicious transactions are also being monitored in coordination with relevant authorities to identify fraud networks.
Government allowances and other forms of assistance are now being transferred digitally and directly to beneficiaries’ accounts, he added.

item.title: Satkhira municipality fails to ensure safe water for households
item.description:
Residents of Satkhira municipality have complained that the water supplied by the local authorities is often contaminated with dirt, foul-smelling substances, and even worms, making it unfit for drinking and household use.
Many families are consequently forced to spend Tk1,500-2,000 a month buying drinking water. Against this backdrop, civil society representatives have proposed eight recommendations to address the crisis, particularly in low-income communities.
The proposals include making water supply services affordable, promoting rooftop rainwater harvesting and household wells, developing rainwater reservoirs, and installing public water taps in slums and densely populated areas.
They also called for protecting ponds and other water bodies from encroachment, regularly testing municipal and jarred water for arsenic, iron, salinity and pH levels, and publishing the results online.
The recommendations were presented at a citizens' dialogue titled “Safe Drinking Water Crisis among Low-income Urban Communities and Ways Forward”, organised by research organisation Barcik at the Mangrove Conference Hall in Satkhira town yesterday.
Satkhira Green Coalition President Abu Affan Roj Babu chaired the event, while municipal Water Supply Engineer Nimai Chandra Pal attended as the chief guest.
At the dialogue, Baddipur Colony residents Jahanara Khatun and Mariam Khatun said their neighbourhood remains waterlogged for nearly six months during the rainy season, causing an acute shortage of drinking water. Many households have yet to receive municipal water connections despite living within the city.
Professor Pabitra Mohan Das said he spends Tk1,600-1,700 a month buying jarred water for drinking and cooking. With an adequate municipal supply, the same needs could be met for around Tk200, he added.

item.title: Kremlin slams Zelensky for divulging US land-for-Nato offer
item.description:
Russia on Monday criticized Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelensky for revealing Washington had proposed that Kyiv cede land for Nato membership as part of a possible peace deal with Moscow.
The Kremlin did not confirm the proposal had been made or comment on it. But Moscow has long opposed Ukraine joining the US-led military alliance.
“We continue to maintain our position that it is inadvisable to disclose details of the discussions taking place between us and the Americans in the interests of the peace process,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters, including AFP.
Zelensky had told journalists on Friday that the offer had been made by US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, who last week held talks in Abu Dhabi with both sides, before separate meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Zelensky.
“The Americans raised a question: ‘What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?’ This was the first time this had been raised,” Zelensky said.
Kyiv has long pushed for Nato membership hoping its mutual defense clauses will be a guarantee against a future Russian attack.
But Moscow has for years railed against new countries joining Nato -- believing it was promised by the United States that that alliance would not move closer to its borders.
Since it launched its full-scale offensive on Ukraine in 2022, both Sweden and Finland - which has a 1,300-kilometre (800-mile) border with Russia -- have joined Nato.

item.title: Death-row convict found hanging in Kashimpur prison
item.description:
A death-row convict in two murder cases was found hanging inside Kashimpur High-Security Central Prison in Gazipur early Monday.
The deceased, Farhad, 41, was the son of the late Hafiz Uddin of Shalinapara village in Tangail Sadar upazila.
Senior Jail Superintendent Mohammad Abdullah-Al-Mamun confirmed the incident, saying Farhad's body was discovered at around 1am in a ground-floor cell of the prison's Himel Building.
He said prison authorities had completed a routine headcount on Sunday before locking the cells for the night. Farhad, who had been sentenced to death for the murder of a man and a woman in Tangail, was sharing the cell with two co-accused.
During the night, the two inmates found him hanging from a cell window with a towel tied around his neck, the superintendent said.
Prison officials were alerted, recovered Farhad and rushed him to Gazipur Shaheed Tajuddin Ahmad Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared him dead on arrival.
An inquest has been conducted, and the body will be handed over to the family after an autopsy, he added. Relatives have arrived at the prison.
The superintendent said Farhad was transferred to Kashimpur High-Security Prison from Dhaka Central Jail in Keraniganj on August 26, 2019.
He was being held in connection with two separate murder cases filed with Tangail police station, in which he had received death sentences.
Abdullah-Al-Mamun also said Farhad had been suffering from various health problems, including severe headaches and visual hallucinations, for around a year. He had received medical treatment at the prison hospital several times.

item.title: Chinmoy Krishna shifted from Chittagong jail to Keraniganj special prison
item.description:
Chinmoy Krishna Das Brahmachari, spokesperson for the Sanatani Jagaran Jote, has been transferred from Chittagong Central Jail to a special prison in Keraniganj, Dhaka.
He was transferred under tight security at around 5am on Monday (November 16), Chittagong Central Jail Senior Jail Superintendent Iqbal Hossain confirmed to Dhaka Tribune.
“Chinmoy Krishna Das has been taken to the special prison in Keraniganj, Dhaka,” he said, adding that he could not provide further details about the reasons for the sudden transfer.
Prison sources said Ranganath Das Brahmachari, who prepares meals for Chinmoy, was not transferred with him and remains at Chittagong Central Jail.
On October 31, 2024, Firoz Khan, then general secretary of the BNP's Mohra Ward unit in Chandgaon, filed a sedition case with Kotwali police against Chinmoy Krishna Das and 18 others over allegations of disrespecting the national flag.
Chinmoy was arrested in Dhaka on November 25, 2024, in connection with the case.
The following day, a Chittagong court rejected his bail petition and ordered him sent to jail. His supporters subsequently surrounded the prison van and staged protests on the court premises. Police fired sound grenades to disperse them before taking him to jail.
During the unrest, several motorcycles and vehicles were vandalised near the court. Later, lawyer Saiful Islam Alif was hacked and beaten to death near Rangam Convention Hall, allegedly by supporters of Chinmoy.
On November 29, 2024, Alif's father, Jamal Uddin, filed a murder case with Kotwali Police Station. The case statement named 31 people and accused another 15 to 16 unidentified individuals.
After completing the investigation, Assistant Commissioner of Chittagong Metropolitan Police (Kotwali) Mahfuzur Rahman submitted a charge sheet on July 1, 2025, naming 38 people as accused. Chinmoy Krishna Das was named as the prime accused.

item.title: Police fire tear gas, sound grenades as garment workers protest in Gazipur
item.description:
Workers from two garment factories staged protests in Gazipur's Konabari area on Monday morning, prompting police to fire tear gas shells and sound grenades to disperse them.
The workers began protesting at around 8am after refusing to join work.
Police and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel have been deployed at key points across the industrial zone to maintain law and order.
Meanwhile, at least 13 garment factories have been declared closed indefinitely since Sunday amid labour unrest and security concerns.
Police said workers from ABM Fashion and Jamuna factories in Konabari gathered outside their workplaces and staged protests, blocking the Konabari-Kashimpur road.
On receiving information, police and BGB personnel asked the workers to clear the road. However, the workers became agitated, prompting law enforcement personnel to fire tear gas shells and sound grenades to disperse them. The workers later left the area, bringing the situation back to normal.
Mohammad Amzad Hossain, superintendent of police of Gazipur Industrial Police-2, said workers from ABM Fashion and Jamuna factories gathered outside their workplaces and staged protests.
"Police fired tear gas shells and sound grenades to disperse the workers and bring the situation under control," he said, adding that police and BGB personnel remain deployed across the industrial zone.

item.title: 10 platoons BGB deployed in Gopalganj
item.description:
The Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has deployed a total of 10 platoons in key areas of Gopalganj district to maintain law and order and ensure public security.
Armoured Personnel Carriers (APCs) have also been deployed to deal with any untoward situation and carry out riot control operations if necessary.
The information was disclosed by the media department of BGB headquarters on Monday morning.
According to the BGB, body-worn cameras have been attached to the maximum possible number of deployed personnel to directly monitor and coordinate their activities on the ground.
Live footage of field operations is also being collected and monitored using drone technology and improvised devices. The BGB headquarters' monitoring cell is closely overseeing these activities and the overall security situation to ensure prompt action in the event of any untoward incident.
Under the Ministry of Home Affairs' directive, BGB personnel have been deployed under the "In Aid to Civil Power" framework at key locations across the district, based on requests and advice from the district magistrate.
In coordination with other law enforcement agencies, they are monitoring the overall security situation and taking necessary measures to protect public life and property.
Leaders and activists of the activities-banned Awami League and its affiliated organisations staged a major show of force in Gopalganj on Sunday, marching openly with sharp weapons, vandalising a police vehicle and public installations, and setting fire to the July Memorial, as the government transferred the district's deputy commissioner and superintendent of police following the unrest.
The processions saw activists carrying machetes, axes, spears, sticks and oars through major streets of the district town, according to eyewitnesses and local reports.
Despite a heavy deployment of law enforcement personnel, the demonstrators marched through several areas, reopened the long-closed district Awami League office and damaged public property.

item.title: Indefinite transport strike in Sylhet withdrawn
item.description:
Transport workers in Sylhet have called off an indefinite strike that was scheduled to begin across the district at 6am Monday, following a meeting with police officials.
Leaders of the Sylhet District Bus, Minibus, Coach and Microbus Workers' Union withdrew the strike at 9pm on Sunday after a meeting at the office of the Sylhet Metropolitan Police Commissioner at his request.
Moinul Islam, president of the union, confirmed the decision at 10:45pm.
Earlier, the strike was announced at a meeting held at the union office in Babna Point, South Surma, on Saturday afternoon under the banner of the Sylhet District Road Transport Owners and Workers Coordination Council.
The workers had called the strike to press three demands.
These include the withdrawal of cases filed against workers' leaders over the deaths of two workers at Kadamtali Terminal; the allocation of designated parking spaces for auto-rickshaws, easy-bikes, legunas and microbuses, alongside the removal of battery-run rickshaws, easy-bikes and tomtoms from the city; and the provision of bank challan numbers for CNG-run auto-rickshaws.

Dhaka air 3rd worst in world Monday morning
item.description:
Dhaka's air quality remained ‘very unhealthy’ on Monday morning, with an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 208 at 9:10am.
With this score, the capital ranked third among the world's most polluted cities.
A ‘very unhealthy’ air quality level means people, regardless of their health condition, may experience more serious health effects from air pollution. Even short-term exposure can affect anyone.
Pakistan's Lahore topped the list with an AQI score of 306, followed by India's Kolkata with 255.
Earlier, at 8:30am on Sunday, Dhaka also ranked third among the world's most polluted cities, with an AQI score of 206.
According to the AQI scale, readings of 101-150 are considered unhealthy for sensitive groups, while scores of 151-200 indicate unhealthy air quality. Readings of 201-300 are classified as very unhealthy, while scores above 300 are considered hazardous and pose serious health risks.
The AQI measures daily air quality, indicating pollution levels and their potential effects on public health.
In Bangladesh, air quality is assessed based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulphur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
The World Health Organization (WHO) estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths worldwide each year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.
